comment: D-STATE-1. One `{id, name, at}` record -- the shape `recents[]`,
`lastPlayed` and `session` all share -- run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js
(Model.playedRecord, through parseState) and tests/test_state.py
(normalize_played). A rule implemented in two languages gets one fixture.
This file exists because the two DID disagree. Model.js coerces with
Math.trunc(Number(x)), which parses the whole JavaScript numeric grammar;
the helper used int(x), which accepts only a plain integer literal and
raises on everything else, falling through to 0. Same bytes, two answers.
Found by the saved-search fixture, which included `at: "12.9"` for its own
key and went red on a key it was not written for -- the shared-fixture rule
working on a rule nobody had applied it to yet.
The agreed answer is Model.js's, for two reasons. It is the reader the
guide runs, so it is what the user's screen already reflects; and it is the
more tolerant of the two, so adopting it cannot turn a value that used to
be read into one that is not.
D-STATE-4. The fix for D-STATE-1 was float() then int(), which bought
Python's grammar, not JavaScript's, and raised OverflowError on an infinite
number, so every helper state verb that reads the file ended `internal`. Neither engine's
Number() is one grammar either (V4 reads "inf" as Infinity and node NaN;
V4 trims U+0085 and node U+FEFF). So both readers now share an explicit one
(storedInt in model/state.mjs, coerce_int). A JSON number is its value and a boolean 1
or 0. A string is read only as a decimal literal of at most 64 code units
once the reader's class (url-whitespace.json) is off its ends. The answer is truncated toward zero,
and anything else, or anything not finite, is 0. The D-STATE-4 vectors
below say which reader each one moved.
`atText` holds JSON tokens a fixture value cannot carry. Each runner
splices the token into a document's text and parses that, as each reader
parses state.json. V4's JSON.parse refuses a number past the double range,
whole file and all (D-STATE-5), so these run in node and python only.
